source: Mumford (1992) On the computational architecture of the neocortex II
finding: Mumford extended retina/LGN redundancy removal into a general cortical theory. Higher areas send down templates; lower areas send up only the residual after fitting the template. No simulations were given.
limits: Described second-hand via the Millidge review; Mumford paper itself not opened.
agent_relevance: Origin of the 'send the residual, not the signal' idea. Background only.

source: Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2022) Predictive coding: a theoretical and experimental review
finding: The review dates predictive coding to Srinivasan, Laughlin and Dubs (1982) for retina, Mumford (1992) for cortex, and Rao and Ballard (1999) for the first working network. Friston (2003-2008) recast the Rao and Ballard energy function as variational free energy, so the learning rules become approximate Bayesian inference.
quote: They created a small predictive coding network according to the principles identified by Mumford
limits: Historical account by authors who work on the theory; not an independent test.
agent_relevance: Shows the lineage: efficient-coding idea, then working model, then Bayesian formalism. Our scaffold borrows none of the neural detail.

source: Rao and Ballard (1999) Predictive coding in the visual cortex: a functional interpretation of some extra-classical receptive-field effects
finding: Feedback connections carry predictions of lower-level activity; feedforward connections carry residual errors. Trained on natural images, a hierarchical network developed simple-cell-like receptive fields. The error-carrying subset showed endstopping and other extra-classical effects.
numbers: No sample numbers read (abstract only, via Europe PMC).
quote: rather than being exclusively feedforward phenomena, nonclassical surround effects in the visual cortex may also result from cortico-cortical feedback
limits: Only the abstract was read. A simulation, not a recording; endstopping is also explained by feedforward models.
agent_relevance: The founding working model. Shows top-down prediction plus bottom-up residual can be a full learning system.

source: Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2022) Predictive coding: a theoretical and experimental review
finding: Endstopping is the key explained phenomenon. A classical feedforward feature detector could not respond to a bar ending just outside its field. In the predictive coding net, the top-down prediction of the bar's continuation is violated at the end and an error unit fires. Prediction, inference and weight updates all follow from gradient descent on one energy function.
limits: Explanation is a model fit; alternatives are not ruled out by it.
agent_relevance: A single objective that drives inference and learning is the design appeal. Our schema uses code-checked rules instead.

source: Murray, Kersten, Olshausen, Schrater, Woods (2004) Perceptual grouping and the interactions between visual cortical areas
finding: fMRI: when visual elements formed coherent shapes versus random arrangements, activity rose in higher object area LOC and fell in V1. Read as higher-area grouping reducing early-area activity, consistent with predictive coding and 'explaining away'.
numbers: No numbers read (abstract only). The earlier 2002 PNAS study with the same design was not opened.
quote: significant activity increases in the LOC and concurrent reductions of activity in V1 when elements formed coherent shapes
limits: Abstract only. BOLD sums error and prediction units so sign is ambiguous; attention differences are a rival cause.
agent_relevance: Classic human evidence that top-down structure lowers low-level response.

source: Walsh, McGovern, Clark, O'Connell (2020) Evaluating the neurophysiological evidence for predictive processing as a model of perception
finding: Review tests four core hypotheses against neurophysiology. Many studies show the predicted expectation effects, but a significant contingent failed to replicate them. Overall support is mixed, and clear-cut counterevidence has not emerged.
numbers: Hypotheses: 1) error responses scale inversely with expectation; 2) expectations shape sensory representations; 3) distinct error and prediction subpopulations; 4) expectation effects at contiguous hierarchy levels.
quote: on the whole it must be concluded that the empirical support for each of PP's key hypotheses is mixed
limits: Narrative review, not a quantitative meta-analysis.
agent_relevance: The theory is hard to falsify; hold 'the brain does PP' loosely. Use as design analogy only.

source: Summerfield, Trittschuh, Monti, Mesulam, Egner (2008) Neural repetition suppression reflects fulfilled perceptual expectations (as described in Walsh 2020)
finding: fMRI in fusiform face area: expected face repetitions gave much smaller BOLD responses than unexpected ones, which argues against pure neural adaptation.
numbers: Exact effect sizes not given in the review.
limits: Seen only through Walsh 2020. Original not opened.
agent_relevance: Key support for expectation suppression beyond adaptation.

source: Kaliukhovich and Vogels (2011) (as described in Walsh 2020)
finding: Attempted replication in macaque IT single cells. Responses to deviant stimuli were indistinguishable from responses to rare but conditionally probable stimuli, so no expectation effect beyond stimulus frequency.
limits: Stimuli were unfamiliar to monkeys and the task was passive fixation; both may weaken expectation effects. Seen second-hand.
agent_relevance: A failed replication of the founding expectation suppression result, with plausible boundary conditions (familiarity, attention).

source: Walsh, McGovern, Clark, O'Connell (2020) Evaluating the neurophysiological evidence for predictive processing as a model of perception
finding: Direct recordings split. Bell et al. found unexpected stimuli raised responses, but other studies in macaque IT and rodent V1 found unexpected or random stimuli gave reduced responses relative to expected ones. It is also disputed whether suppression tracks nonadjacent sequence regularities or only the previous stimulus.
limits: Mixed direction of effect weakens simple error-unit claims.
agent_relevance: Evidence base is contested; do not import the theory as a claim of mechanism.

source: Kok, Bains, van Mourik, Norris, de Lange (2016) 7T laminar fMRI of Kanizsa illusory figures (as described in Walsh 2020)
finding: 7T fMRI: illusory figures raised activation in deep V1 layers, while responses to the predictable Pac-Man inducers were dampened in superficial and middle layers, matching a bottom-up laminar profile.
limits: Unclear why missing input at the illusory contour did not itself trigger an error response in superficial layers.
agent_relevance: Laminar support for deep-layer predictions and superficial errors, with open puzzles.

source: Bastos, Usrey, Adams, Mangun, Fries, Friston (2012) Canonical microcircuits for predictive coding
finding: Process theory mapping: superficial pyramidal cells (L2/3) carry forward prediction errors; deep pyramidal cells (L5/6) hold expectations that send feedback predictions; L4 spiny stellate cells receive feedforward input. Precision acts as gain on superficial error cells, linked to attention. Feedback should be inhibitory and modulatory.
numbers: Cited data: optogenetic L6 activation in V1 cut responses 76% in LGN and about 80-84% in V1 (Olsen 2012). Superficial layers show more gamma, deep layers more alpha/beta (Maier 2010; Buffalo 2011).
quote: must encode and broadcast prediction errors on hidden causes
limits: Read only the first 100k of 187k characters. Mapping is a proposal; some required connections are only predicted.
agent_relevance: Gives layer-level testable predictions; this is what makes it a process theory rather than a slogan.

source: Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2022) Predictive coding: a theoretical and experimental review
finding: Evidence for expectation suppression is hard to interpret. Repetition and expectation suppression are well established at unit level but are also explained by neural adaptation. BOLD fMRI results are mixed, and the theory does not clearly predict regional BOLD because error units, prediction units and precision all add up.
limits: Authors note high precision for predicted stimuli could boost error units and offset the drop.
agent_relevance: Warns that aggregate measures cannot test the theory cleanly.

source: Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2022) Predictive coding: a theoretical and experimental review
finding: Error units may not be separate cells. Some versions use multicompartment neurons with an apical dendrite holding the error, so failing to find explicit error units would not refute the theory. Authors say flexibility of theory and process theory makes it hard to confirm or refute.
limits: Authors' own admission of low falsifiability.
agent_relevance: Supports treating the framework as a design pattern, not a verified mechanism.

source: Whittington and Bogacz (2017) An approximation of the error backpropagation algorithm in a predictive coding network with local Hebbian synaptic plasticity
finding: A predictive coding network learns supervised tasks with only local Hebbian plasticity. For certain parameters its weight change converges to backprop. First demonstration of near-equivalence to backprop.
numbers: On MNIST, comparison networks reached training error 0.00% and validation error 1.7% to 1.8% (20 inference steps). Learning rate not tuned for validation.
limits: Small MLP only. Equivalence holds only under conditions; needs inference iterations before each update.
agent_relevance: Backprop-like learning from local rules; the theory as an engineering learning algorithm.

source: Song, Lukasiewicz, Xu, Bogacz (2020) Can the brain do backpropagation? Exact implementation of backpropagation in predictive coding networks
finding: A model that produces exactly the same weight updates as backprop with local plasticity, plus a variant that works autonomously.
numbers: No numbers read (abstract only). The Millidge review states the first iteration equals backprop if initialised at the feedforward pass.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Equivalence means no new capability over backprop.

source: Millidge, Tschantz, Buckley (2020) Predictive coding approximates backprop along arbitrary computation graphs
finding: At the equilibrium of one global free energy on any directed acyclic computation graph, error units equal the backprop gradients, using local connectivity and Hebbian updates for parameter-linear functions. Tested on CNNs, RNNs and LSTMs.
numbers: Scalar test v_L = tan(theta v0)+sin(v0^2), v0=5, theta=2, target 3: converged to autodiff gradients, stable up to inference learning rate 0.5; exact gradients within 100 iterations. CNN on SVHN, CIFAR10, CIFAR100 (5 seeds) and LSTM on Shakespeare gave performance largely indistinguishable from backprop. About 100x higher compute from 100-200 inference iterations.
limits: Small models, below state of the art. Transformers and ResNets named as future work, not done.
agent_relevance: Parity with backprop at about 100x cost: no reason to use it in a scaffold. The claim is about brain plausibility.

source: Millidge, Tschantz, Seth, Buckley (2020) Activation relaxation: a local dynamical approximation to backpropagation in the brain
finding: A simpler dynamical scheme without separate error units. Tested on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST with a 4-layer MLP, 5 seeds, 100 inference iterations per step, which closely approximated backprop gradients. Feedback alignment with random weights converged to lower accuracy.
numbers: Exact accuracies not recorded in this pass.
limits: Small image benchmarks only.
agent_relevance: More evidence that the algorithmic core is gradient descent by relaxation.

source: Lotter, Kreiman, Cox (2017) Deep predictive coding networks for video prediction and unsupervised learning (PredNet)
finding: PredNet is a stack of layers that each predict the layer below and pass only errors upward. It beat a matched CNN-LSTM encoder-decoder and a copy-last-frame baseline at next-frame prediction.
numbers: Rotating faces (MSE/SSIM): PredNet L0 0.0152/0.937; Lall 0.0157/0.921; CNN-LSTM 0.0180/0.907; copy last 0.125/0.631. CalTech Pedestrian: L0 3.13e-3/0.884; Lall 3.33e-3/0.875; CNN-LSTM 3.67e-3/0.865; copy last 7.95e-3/0.762. Over four other hyperparameter sets L0 cut error 14.7% (MSE) and 14.9% (SSIM) on average.
limits: Trained on KITTI, tested on CalTech. Gain over matched control is modest. Not a language model.
agent_relevance: Sending errors up beats sending activations up, modestly; the idea transfers to prediction but not hugely.

source: Lotter, Kreiman, Cox (2017) PredNet (representation test)
finding: Representations learned by predicting frames support a downstream task with little labelled data: linear readout of steering angle on Comma.ai data.
numbers: With 1K labelled examples, linear readout of PredNet L0 explained 74% of steering-angle variance and beat the CNN-LSTM by 35%. With 25K examples MSE 2.14 deg^2, versus about 4 for a CNN trained end to end on 396K examples (single frame).
limits: Lall variant underperformed L0 here, so loss weighting changes what is learned.
agent_relevance: Predicting the next input is a cheap source of useful features.

source: Caucheteux, Gramfort, King (2023) Evidence of a predictive coding hierarchy in the human brain listening to speech
finding: Adding GPT-2 forecast representations of upcoming words improved fMRI brain scores. Best forecast distance was 8 words (about 3.15 s). Frontal and parietal cortex forecast further and with deeper, more contextual representations than temporal cortex, as a hierarchy predicts.
numbers: 304 participants, 27 stories, about 4 to 4.6 h of stimulus. Peak brain score R = 0.23 in superior temporal sulcus, about 60% of noise ceiling. Forecast gain 23% (+-9% across individuals). Inferior frontal gyrus forecasts 0.9 +-0.2 words further than anterior STS (P<0.001). Angular gyrus vs Heschl's gyri differ by 2.5 +-0.3 layers (P<0.001).
limits: fMRI resolution about 1.5 s. Correlational: shows LLM forecasts relate linearly to brain activity, not that the brain computes errors. Authors call the tested architecture rudimentary and its NLP utility untested.
agent_relevance: Best LLM-linked test of a hierarchy of predictions at different time scales. Suggests multi-horizon prediction signals add information.

source: Caucheteux, Gramfort, King (2023) (syntax vs semantics and fine-tuning)
finding: Semantic forecasts were long-range and spread over frontal and parietal lobes; syntactic forecasts were short-range and local to superior temporal and left frontal areas. Fine-tuning GPT-2 to predict a deeper layer 8 words ahead raised frontoparietal brain scores.
numbers: Semantic d* = 8 words; syntactic d* = 5 words. Fine-tuning gave over 2% mean frontoparietal brain-score gain (P<0.001); auditory and low-level areas gained nothing significant.
limits: Gain is small (about 2%). No task-accuracy result.
agent_relevance: Hints a multi-level, multi-horizon objective matches brain data better. No evidence it improves task accuracy.

source: Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2022) Predictive coding: a theoretical and experimental review
finding: Unsupervised predictive coding nets act as decoder-only autoencoders: latent states come from iterative inference (the E step) instead of an encoder. On MNIST, the latent code separates the ten digits under PCA though learned without labels (Millidge 2019). Temporal variants predict the next input.
limits: Small datasets in the reported works.
agent_relevance: Iterative inference over latent states resembles scaffolds that refine an answer in loops, but no LLM result here.

source: Keller and Mrsic-Flogel (2018) Predictive processing: a canonical cortical computation (cited in Millidge review)
finding: Cited as a source of process-theory tests in mouse visual cortex; the review flags an open question about what opponent error populations would signify.
limits: Not opened; named only.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2022) Predictive coding: a theoretical and experimental review
finding: Open issues: error units need both positive and negative signalling, weights must be symmetric between prediction and error pathways, and inference is a slow iterative loop. Deep layers use slower alpha/beta rhythms and superficial layers faster gamma (Bastos 2015), as the theory predicts for predictions versus errors.
limits: Biological plausibility partly unresolved.
agent_relevance: These constraints explain why predictive coding is slow in silicon.

source: Walsh, McGovern, Clark, O'Connell (2020) Evaluating the neurophysiological evidence for predictive processing as a model of perception
finding: Low-level versus high-level error in auditory oddball work: a low-level prediction error was an early gamma increase over primary auditory cortex to local deviants. A higher-level error was a late gamma increase over anterior temporal cortex to local and global deviants.
limits: Many studies struggle to show systematic effects across contiguous hierarchy levels (Hypothesis 4).
agent_relevance: Hierarchical claim only partly supported.

source: Walsh, McGovern, Clark, O'Connell (2020) Evaluating the neurophysiological evidence for predictive processing as a model of perception
finding: Studies often credit whole-population response changes to error signals while ignoring that prediction units are active too. Expectation effects depend on attention via precision weighting; PP predicts an expectation-by-attention interaction that the feedforward account does not.
limits: Attention confound can mimic or hide prediction effects.
agent_relevance: Any 'prediction error' claim must control for what is attended.
